# Summary of the Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997

## Overview
The 1997 SNP Manifesto, titled "Yes We Can — Win the Best for Scotland," presented a comprehensive plan for Scottish independence under the leadership of Alex Salmond. The document outlined the SNP's vision for a self-governing Scotland as a full member of the European Union.

## Core Arguments for Independence
The manifesto contested several myths about Scottish independence, asserting that Scotland was a wealthy nation subsidizing London by £27 billion over 18 years. It argued Scotland would automatically become an EU member upon independence, maintain open borders with England, and protect existing pensions and investments. The SNP positioned independence as the "normal status" for nations, noting that over 50 countries had gained independence from Britain since 1945.

## Path to Independence
The SNP proposed that upon electing a majority of SNP MPs, negotiations would begin with the UK government over 6-12 months, followed by a referendum to approve the independence settlement. A new constitution would establish citizens' rights, a proportionally-elected parliament, and protected local government powers.

## Economic Policies
The manifesto included ambitious economic proposals: reducing corporation tax from 33% to 30%, cutting small company rates from 23% to 18%, abolishing certain National Insurance contributions, and introducing a 15p starter income tax rate. The SNP pledged to create 100,000 new jobs and establish Scotland as internationally competitive while maintaining fiscal responsibility by repaying £6.6 billion of inherited national debt over four years.

## Social Priorities
Key social commitments included increasing Child Benefit to £12.50 weekly, raising state pensions, introducing a Cold Climate Allowance, abolishing means testing for elderly care, and restoring benefits for 16-17 year olds. The manifesto promised to abolish the NHS internal market, add £35 million annually to health spending, and implement a comprehensive housing program to eliminate homelessness and build 20,000 affordable homes.

## Education and Services
Educational priorities included free nursery education for all 3-4 year olds, 700 additional teachers, restored student grants, and universal internet access in schools. The SNP also pledged to return water services to democratic control and protect local government autonomy.

## Defence and International Relations
The manifesto outlined plans for Scottish Defence Forces comprising approximately 20,000 regular personnel, committed to removing Trident nuclear weapons, and proposed phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining European security cooperation. Scotland would pursue full UN membership and increase overseas aid toward the 0.7% GDP target.
